description: Import chosen assets from a media url — a page, a direct file link, or a file the user attached in this conversation — straight into the workspace, with no local file and no PUT. Each selection must echo an assetId and qualityId from discover_external_media for the SAME url; invented ids are rejected. One selection produces one media item, so the same asset can be imported twice with different ranges to get two clips. Downloading is asynchronous: poll get_upload until it reports the import finished. Attachment urls usually expire, so import promptly rather than storing the link for later. Returns one media record per selection (id obj_..., name, type, uploaded, externalSource with its download state).

selections.description: One entry per media item to create.

endSeconds.description: Seconds into the source where the clip ends, after startSeconds. Omitted: the end of the source.

preciseCut.description: Cut exactly at the offsets (re-encodes, markedly slower) instead of snapping to the nearest keyframe, which may include a few extra seconds at the start.

startSeconds.description: Seconds into the source where the clip starts. Omitted: the beginning of the source.

url.description: The SAME url passed to discover_external_media.

name: import_upload_from_url

code.description: Stable — branch on it: INVALID_INPUT, REVISION_REQUIRED, STALE_PUBLISH, CONFIRM_REQUIRED, UNAVAILABLE, …

currentRevision.description: CONFLICT: the revision it has now

detail.description: What is wrong, in a sentence

errors.description: Each problem, when a check refused it

title: Import media from a URL
